note: This folder is mostly hand-maintained static content (README, RUN.md, index.html, run.sh, process/, schemas/, config/, examples/, assets/, LICENSE, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, wiki/, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, hooks/hooks.json, commands/). assets/ holds site screenshots (e.g. site-hero.png) used by README.md/wiki pages, -- the shared presentation layer that briefly lived there (assets/report.css, assets/report.js, assets/fonts/) was removed once the plate design moved into the renderer itself, so every example page is self-contained exactly like the file bar report writes. examples/ holds real tool output plus the capture it was measured from: examples/capture/ carries the seven transcripts and a run.sh that rebuilds every deterministic example in three commands. hooks/hooks.json is a byte-identical copy of bar_hook::plugin_hooks_json()'s output, drift-guarded by bar-hook/tests/plugin_drift.rs in the private working repo -- not hand-edited here, but not generated by public-export.sh either. Only CRATES.md is generated by scripts/public-export.sh, from the private working repo's crate manifests. Requires human approval (ADR-016) before this folder is pushed to a real GitHub remote.
recent_changes: 2026-08-20 (independent pre-merge review, six defects fixed, version bumped 0.2.0 -> 0.2.1): an independent review of the report-example redesign + measurement-bug-fix PR (merged as commit 914dd14c) found and fixed six further issues before merging, beyond the PR's own ADR-129/130/131 work described in the entries below. (1) Script injection: tool names from the transcript reached an inline <script> block via HTML-only escaping in every generated report -- fixed with proper JSON escaping and DOM-safe (textContent) rendering in the shared plate JS runtime. (2) The blind-store honesty guarantee ADR-128/129 exist to deliver failed on exactly the input it was written for: a legacy/offloaded-only store rendered confidently clean instead of flagged blind -- fixed by deriving the flag from run coverage, not scan hits. (3) Offloading a large tool_use.input silently zeroed six detectors (rework, hotspots, agent spawns, skill usage, TodoWrite, task ledger) because the size cap discarded the whole call's identity along with its payload -- fixed with a declared per-tool-type bulk-subfield list, so only the oversized field is trimmed. (4) HUB.aisp asserted a false equation inside its own self-certifying evidence block (31 tables claimed to equal 29, real count 32) and was missing correlation_stats from its routing map -- fixed and re-verified against a freshly migrated store via a real schema dump, not just cross-referenced migration files. (5) Re-ingest, the documented remedy for a partial validation caveat, silently double-counted instead of fixing anything, from two independent causes: a migration back-fill/live-ingest line-number mismatch, and NULL defeating a UNIQUE constraint on run-less ingest -- both fixed with one mechanism, clearing a turn's facts before re-deriving them (ADR-131). (6) pytest's verdict matcher accepted plain prose (e.g. 'The deploy failed in staging...') as a test result -- the guard test written for exactly this case asserted the acceptance rather than the refusal; fixed, and the test corrected to assert the refusal it was meant to. cargo test --workspace: 699 green (0 failed, 6 ignored) at merge time; checksums and scripts/public-export.sh --check both verified clean before and after. Version bumped 0.2.0 -> 0.2.1 across the workspace, bar-mcp, bar-observatory, and the plugin/marketplace manifests -- a patch release, since no crate's public CLI surface or config schema changed. All 16 crates are now live on crates.io at 0.2.1 (verified via the crates.io API and a real cargo install --locked from the published registry, then a genuine init/ingest/report/doctor run against the installed binary). The GitHub push to github.com/bar181/bar-observatory has not happened yet for this version; that remains the one standing human-approval gate on this repo. Earlier entries preserved below. Also found while staging this release: the shipped deterministic example's own renderer_version had been stale at 0.1.1 -- two patch releases behind -- because the examples had been regenerated from data without a fresh cargo build --release afterward. Rebuilt from a genuinely fresh 0.2.1 binary; the field-for-field diff against the previously-shipped example was exactly the four fields expected to move on any regeneration (renderer_version, source_db_hash, template_hash, and the report.id derived from the hash) -- no measured figure changed. New example id barobs-14fd056be293, propagated to every current cross-reference (examples/README.html, the four hand-assembled report pages, wiki/human-html/report-guide.html, bar-obs-private/report-scorecard.html); the id in this file's own earlier dated entries and in CHANGELOG.md's [0.2.0] entry was deliberately left as barobs-801e4778ddff -- those are a record of what was true when they were written, not live claims. 2026-08-19 (Markdown parity pass): the report scorecard's top finding was that Markdown is a second-class citizen -- four of five pages strongest in HTML and flatter in Markdown, though Markdown is the copy that lands in a pull request, and the generated report had fifteen sections with no way to move between them while its HTML twin had a numbered plate rail. to_markdown now emits a numbered contents index derived from the document's own headings, so it cannot drift out of step with the sections that exist, with anchors following GitHub's real slug rule including Evidence & integrity -> #evidence--integrity; the three hand-built example reports got the same index. Two defects in the shipped HTML surfaced while pinning that down, both visible to a reader: the plate rail double-escaped its labels (Evidence &amp; integrity on screen) and leaked the entity into the section's own anchor (#evidence-amp-integrity). Four sections were also named differently in the two formats -- a chip in HTML, a parenthetical in Markdown -- so the two disagreed about what section 11 was called; they are now identical in both, chip preserved, and Cost's two different Markdown titles were unified with HTML's one. A new test asserts the index and the rail agree on every section number and label, that every anchor resolves, and that the ampersand case anchors the way GitHub does. The internal REPORT-SCORECARD.md became report-scorecard.html: it scored four reports on design while itself being Markdown, and the repository's own rule is that no score lives in more than one file, so it moved rather than being duplicated -- built in the same plate system, with one departure recorded in its stylesheet, that the two layer accents sit dE 7.5 apart under normal vision (below the categorical floor), so its meters encode magnitude in one hue and layer identity stays written, the rule the reports already follow. All example screenshots regenerated including management-read.png, which had gone stale. cargo test --workspace green at 685; new example id barobs-801e4778ddff. Earlier entries preserved below. 2026-08-19 (ADR-131): adversarial probes over the ADR-129/130 fixes found a defect in one of them. Both ADRs removed a silent undercount that flattered the session, and both shipped new counting code; a probe suite asked that new code the same question. Two findings. (1) validation_facts was keyed UNIQUE(run_id, seq, evidence_line) with INSERT OR IGNORE, so two byte-identical verdict lines in one tool result collapsed to one row -- and that is not a contrived shape, because cargo test --workspace emits one test result: line per crate and every doc-test-free crate emits identical bytes, so a workspace run under-reported its own verdict count in the flattering direction. Identity is now (run_id, seq, line_no), the line rather than its text; migration 0026 rebuilds the table and back-fills existing rows rather than dropping them. (2) ADR-130 promised the rare structure-lost offload would be counted separately so the real loss is not hidden, but it was counted into an in-memory struct that evaporates at process exit -- the same defect DD-08 fixed for plan_docs, a claimed count no table held. The fallback row now marks itself and the capture-quality row reports it. Six further probes found nothing and are kept as tests: array-shaped content, unlisted envelope fields, mixed-vintage stores, run-less ingest, marker forgery, re-ingest idempotency. The published example capture never contained the shape that triggered the first defect, which is why it survived every earlier pass; re-deriving its figures on the fixed code changes nothing, and that is reported as the confirmation it is rather than as evidence the fix was unnecessary. The originally reported defect was also confirmed end-to-end against the pre-fix binary built from the commit before ADR-129, over a capture matching the reporter's description (5 of 138 tool results offloaded, full pytest runs, verdict at the tail): before, validation read not_observed with the note 'no cargo test result: lines in this transcript's tool outputs' -- the reporter's symptom verbatim, on a session containing five pytest runs; after, observed, 5 verdicts, 4 passed 1 failed, last verdict FAILED. cargo test --workspace green at 680; new example id barobs-801e4778ddff. Earlier entries preserved below. 2026-08-19 (ADR-130): the size cap now offloads the payload and keeps the envelope. ADR-129 disclosed three measurements sharing its blind spot; measuring that blind spot found something worse, in one line of ingest -- an oversized block was not trimmed, it was REPLACED by a {blob_sha} pointer, discarding the fields that identify it. For the fixture's small errored block the discarded envelope is 56 bytes and the pointer that replaced it is 79: the cap threw away structure smaller than the pointer it wrote instead. Measured on a four-result fixture: summary.error_results read 1 where the truth was 2 and bar query errors returned one row instead of two (is_error went with the block, so a failure inside a large output was counted nowhere -- and the biggest outputs are disproportionately the interesting failures); flaky read not_observed, 'none both passed and failed', over a capture where two tests flipped because one run was large; and the transcript channel reported 2 unpaired tool_use/tool_result that did not exist, because tool_use_id went with the block too -- the recorder disclosing a coverage gap it had manufactured, the mirror image of ADR-129's defect, and one that has been inflating that figure on every capture with a large tool result. The fix offloads only the payload field (content for a tool result, input for a call) from a declared per-block-type list rather than 'whichever field is largest', so two structurally identical blocks always store the same way; a block whose envelope alone still exceeds the cap falls back to the bare pointer and is counted separately, so the rare real loss is not hidden behind the common harmless one. Per-test verdict lines live inside the payload and so cannot be reached by keeping the envelope; they get ADR-129's treatment -- extracted at ingest into test_verdict_facts (schema v25), resolved per run, with the same partial-not-none rule. The pre-ADR-130 pointer shape is still recognised so an upgraded binary cannot silently shrink an old store's disclosed gap; existing stores are not rewritten, because a migration that edits captured data is not something this project does, and re-running bar ingest upgrades them. Only two blind scans remain -- the task ledger's 'created successfully' scan and the commit-output scan, both reading output that is short by nature -- stated in wiki/human-md/architecture.md as a floor on their counts rather than left to be discovered. 11 new tests; cargo test --workspace green at 672. The shipped examples were rebuilt (new id barobs-801e4778ddff): the demo capture has no offloaded results, so every measured figure is unchanged, which is itself the cross-check that the new fact path and the old scan agree wherever both can see. Earlier entries preserved below. 2026-08-19 (ADR-129, reported by a user): validation verdicts are extracted at ingest instead of scanned at render. A user reported that validation still read 'not observed' on real sessions despite the 0.2.0 matchers and correctly diagnosed why: long tool outputs are offloaded to the blob store at ingest, so the report-time LIKE search over content_json never sees them, and the excerpt keeps only the head while pytest's verdict is at the tail. Reproduced before designing anything, and the reproduction was worse than the report: a capture with one small passing pytest run and one 16 KB FAILING run rendered as runs:1 passed:1 failed:0 last_ok:true, status observed -- a wrong measurement, not a missing one. Now runs:2 passed:1 failed:1 last_ok:false. The fix is the reporter's own proposal: a new validation_facts table (schema v24) written during ingest while the untruncated output is in hand, so the measurement no longer depends on CONTENT_CAP_BYTES or on where a runner prints its summary. Resolving blobs at render time was explicitly rejected: it is the smaller change and fixes more detectors at once, but it would make bar report depend on a directory the documented single-file copy does not carry, and would fail silently -- a test now renders a copied database with the blob directory absent and asserts identical numbers. Reviewing the ADR before implementing found two holes, both fixed in the ADR rather than in code afterwards: a store holding runs from both vintages could not tell 'ingested before this existed' from 'ran no tests', so resolution is now per run keyed on a recorded marker; and the new text column bypassed the ADR-070 write-seam redaction every other stored text column goes through. No existing store regresses: a pre-v24 capture still reports what the old scan can read, but if it also holds offloaded results the section is partial, never observed, with a reason naming the count and the remedy. The same count is disclosed on the transcript capture-quality row because the failure, flaky and commit scans share the blindness -- they remain blind, stated as a floor on their counts in wiki/human-md/architecture.md rather than left to be discovered. The note also stopped describing every verdict as a cargo 'test result:' line whichever matcher fired. 13 new tests; cargo test --workspace green at 661. The shipped deterministic examples were rebuilt on the fixed renderer (new id barobs-801e4778ddff); the demo capture has no offloaded results, so its 373/344/29 validation figures are unchanged and only the runner attribution and two new honesty fields differ. A self-assessed rubric scorecard for all four example reports was added at bar-obs-private/REPORT-SCORECARD.md, labelled self_reported rather than measured because no real executive or developer has read them.
